title: Nobody can log in
summary: At 06:00 UTC the TLS certificate used by auth‑service expired (notAfter 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z). edge‑gateway has a hard HTTP‑TLS dependency on auth‑service, so every login/token‑refresh request (POST /v1/session) began failing with TLS handshake errors, producing a >10 % error‑rate on the gateway. The gateway config change at 05:52 (keep‑alive timeout) is unrelated.

hypothesis.mechanism: The TLS certificate presented by auth‑service expired at 06:00 UTC. edge‑gateway, which requires a valid TLS handshake for its hard dependency, immediately began failing every request to auth‑service, resulting in 5xx on /v1/session and a spike in gateway error‑rate.
predictions: Replacing the expired certificate on auth‑service will eliminate the TLS handshake errors.
edge‑gateway error‑rate will return to baseline (<0.5 %) after cert replacement.

hypothesis.mechanism: The keep‑alive timeout increase caused downstream connections to stay open longer, leading to timeouts that manifest as 5xx on session routes.
predictions: Reverting the keep‑alive change would restore login success without touching certificates.

hypothesis.mechanism: auth‑service became unhealthy (e.g., process crash) despite passing health checks, causing gateway failures.
predictions: auth‑service logs would show crash or OOM events around 06:00.

hypothesis.mechanism: A network‑level TLS interception or certificate validation change broke the handshake for all callers.
predictions: Other services calling auth‑service over TLS would also see failures.

facts.statement: edge‑gateway calls auth‑service over HTTP with a hard dependency (timeout 1 s).
A config change on edge‑gateway at 05:52:30 UTC raised upstream keep‑alive timeout from 60 s to 75 s.
From 06:00:09 UTC edge‑gateway logs show 1 428 TLS handshake failures: “certificate has expired or is not yet valid (notAfter 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z)”.
auth‑service logs show matching peer errors “remote error: tls: bad certificate” from 06:00:06 UTC onward (1 112 occurrences).
edge‑gateway error‑rate jumps from a baseline 0.2 % to a mean 7.3 % (last 11.6 % at 06:30).
No secret‑rotation, deploy, or other config changes for auth‑service or edge‑gateway in the 05:00‑07:00 window (only chg:2541).
Responder notes that auth‑service pods are up and health checks pass.

assumptions.statement: The “notAfter 2026‑10‑09T06:00:00Z” timestamp in the TLS error accurately reflects the certificate’s expiry time.
assumptions.reason: Log line directly includes the notAfter field; no contradictory evidence.

assumptions.statement: No hidden secret‑rotation or certificate‑renewal job occurred that the change‑history API missed.
assumptions.reason: Change‑history query returned only the gateway config change; tool does not surface cert rotations.

assumptions.statement: Raising the gateway keep‑alive timeout cannot cause TLS handshake failures.
assumptions.reason: Keep‑alive affects connection reuse, not certificate validation; error logs show cert expiry.

assumptions.statement: Health‑check endpoint for auth‑service does not validate the TLS server certificate.
assumptions.reason: Pods report healthy while TLS handshakes fail; typical health checks are HTTP GET on a non‑TLS path.

assumptions.statement: No infrastructure change (network policy, TLS termination) occurred in the window.
assumptions.reason: Change‑history shows none; both services report the same cert‑expiry message.

actions.description: Replace the expired TLS certificate on auth‑service and restart affected pods.
actions.rationale: Directly eliminates the handshake failure identified as root cause (H1).

actions.description: Validate that edge‑gateway logs no longer show TLS handshake errors and that POST /v1/session returns 200 for test accounts.
actions.rationale: Confirms the fix propagates through the hard dependency.

actions.description: Add certificate‑expiry monitoring alerts (30‑day, 7‑day, 1‑day) for all identity‑service certificates.
actions.rationale: Prevents future time‑based expirations from causing outages.

actions.description: Automate certificate rotation (e.g., cert‑manager or secret‑rotation pipeline) so no manual step is required.
actions.rationale: Removes human‑process gap that allowed the cert to expire.

actions.description: Extend auth‑service health check to perform a TLS handshake or verify cert notAfter > now.
actions.rationale: Makes future cert expirations visible to the health‑check system.

actions.description: Ensure secret/cert rotation events are recorded in the change‑history feed.
actions.rationale: Closes visibility gap (G2) for future investigations.
